evidence.text: The county clerk's log records the permit issuance.
A dated photograph shows the posted permit.
Two inspectors confirm the site visit on record.
A mass-mailed flyer claims the permit was revoked; no issuing authority is named.
An unverified tip-line call alleges the donation records are fabricated.
The charity's audited filing lists the donation.
The recipient confirms receipt in writing.
The lab notebook records the calibration run.
A second technician initials the log entry.
A forwarded clip claims the calibration was faked; the clip cites no source.
The instrument's service history shows no anomaly.
The raw data file timestamps match the log.
The shipping manifest lists the cargo as delivered.
The receiving dock signs the delivery receipt.
The carrier's tracking log shows the handoff.
A syndicated column asserts the shipment never arrived; no documents are shown.
The enrollment roster lists the student as registered.
The bursar's receipt confirms tuition paid.
A robocall claims the enrollment database was breached and altered.
The fire marshal's report records the inspection pass.
The building manager confirms the alarm test.
The insurer's surveyor rates the building compliant.
A viral short video claims the inspection was bought; no evidence is offered.
The library log records the book's return.
The librarian confirms the reshelving.
The patron's account shows no outstanding fine.
The zoning map marks the parcel as protected wetland.
The environmental survey confirms the designation.
A realtor's flyer advertises the parcel as buildable.
